question: GTDB-Tk was allocated 16 GB on the strength of a 4 GB 'sampled peak' taken from 60-second sampling. Sampling at 2-5 s found ~37 GiB in a ~30-second spike that the old interval had stepped over. Two things then had to be established before the Enterobacterales and Actinomycetes runs: does the peak scale with genome COUNT (in which case a smaller gtdbtk_shard_size is the fix), and does it scale with taxonomic DIVERSITY (in which case the figure measured on one family says nothing about an order or a phylum-spanning run)?
answer: Neither, in the way that would have mattered. Memory saturates with count by about 100 genomes and is FLAT across diversity: 36.3 GiB for one family, 38.2 for eight families, 38.2 for 29 phyla, all at a fixed 300 genomes. So 40 GB holds for every planned run and sharding is not a memory lever. What diversity does drive is TIME, steeply: the same 300 genomes took 27 min for one family, 2h07m for eight, and over 5h for 29 phyla without finishing. Memory and time have different drivers, and only the memory question gated the allocation.
mechanism: The two costs sit in different stages. MEMORY is the all-vs-all ANI screen: every arm's peak falls inside the ANI window and BEFORE the first pplacer starts (arm C peaked 17:24:59, first pplacer 17:35:56), and arm A ran ZERO pplacer invocations yet still peaked at 36.3 GiB. It saturates with query count rather than being strictly fixed -- 25 genomes cost 10.67 GiB where 100 cost 34.44 -- so the defensible claim is that the plateau is reached by ~100 genomes and is then insensitive to both count and diversity, not that it is a constant reference-sketch load. TIME is pplacer, which is memory-cheap because --scratch_dir spills it to disk (18.4 GB of scratch observed; GTDB-Tk logs 'decreases memory usage and performance'). GTDB-Tk 2.x places against a split reference -- one backbone tree plus 8 class-level subtrees -- and runs pplacer once per subtree holding queries, so breadth sets how many traversals happen.
design: Count and diversity varied separately. COUNT: 25 / 100 / 300 genomes, all Erwiniaceae, same files, flags and database. DIVERSITY: 300 genomes held constant while breadth varied -- 300 Erwiniaceae (1 family), 300 round-robined across Enterobacterales' 8 families, 300 round-robined across 29 phyla of the Bacteria pilot (including 23 Actinomycetota, so Goal 3's clade is bracketed). All arms used the pipeline's own invocation: gtdbtk classify_wf --cpus 8 --pplacer_cpus 1 --min_perc_aa 10 --scratch_dir scratch_tmp, ANI screen ON, against release226. Genomes converted with the pipeline's own scripts/genome/genbank_to_fasta.py and sanitised as the module does. Strictly sequential: two concurrent shards at ~37 GiB would have measured swap.
instruments: Three, because the first two were each wrong in a different way. Nextflow's peak_rss sums RSS across the process tree and so double-counts shared pages -- real for GTDB-Tk (PSS equals RSS) but a 5.5x overstatement for BiG-SCAPE (21 workers sharing a Pfam database, peak_rss 16 GB against PSS 2.9 GiB). Total Pss fixes that but counts clean file-backed mmap pages, which are reclaimable page cache and not a requirement: during one stage it read 54.2 GiB while the kernel simultaneously reported 54.6 GiB AVAILABLE, and the same process showed RSS 54.6 GiB against Pss_Anon 0.76 GiB. The figures here are system mem_used (MemTotal - MemAvailable) corroborated by Pss_Anon, sampled every 2-5 s. A 60 s interval misses this peak entirely, which is how the 4 GB arose.

diversity_series_300_genomes.stopped_because: memory was already answered and flat; the remaining ~3h40m would only have refined a time figure the design overstates anyway

pipeline_run_cross_check.note: ran only because the local executor treats `memory` as an admission constraint it does not enforce

measured.swap: never material -- 0.33 GiB peak across all arms, so no figure here is a swap-capped ceiling

consequences.allocation: GTDBTK_CLASSIFY is allocated 48 GB by name in conf/labels.config. By name rather than through its process_high_memory label -- of which it is the only user -- because a generated machine.config overrides labels. 48 rather than 40: the peak is 38.8 GiB, so 40 GiB leaves 3% headroom on a ~30 s spike whose size tracks the GTDB reference data, and release 232 is already flagged as available. The local executor would only queue differently, but the slurm profile enforces memory as a cgroup where 3% is an OOM kill. 48 GB is also what the profile requested before the 2026-11-02 cut to 16: that original figure was right and the cut was the error.
consequences.concurrency_fixed_for_free: There is no maxForks on GTDBTK_CLASSIFY, so admission is memory arithmetic. At 16 GB a 57 GB box admitted THREE shards demanding ~110 GiB, which any run above gtdbtk_shard_size = 5000 genomes would have triggered. At 40 GB the same arithmetic yields one.
consequences.minimum_spec: GTDB-Tk will not be admitted under ~52 GB. It fails at admission with a clear message rather than being OOM-killed mid-placement; main.nf warns first and check_machine.py proposes run_gtdbtk = false. This workstation (56.9 GB, 50.1 budgetable) still qualifies.
consequences.sharding_is_not_a_memory_lever: 5000 -> 300 would save nothing (36.2 vs 36.8 GiB) and 5000 -> 25 would save 26 GiB at 12x the shards, each paying the ANI screen's ~27-35 min fixed cost over all 143,614 reference genomes.

caveats: THE ARMS OVERSTATE TIME. Round-robining across families oversamples rare lineages -- arm B drew on Gallaecimonadaceae (3 genomes available) and Bruguierivoracaceae (27) beside Enterobacteriaceae -- so its tree-path genomes are maximally novel and expensive to place. A real run samples NCBI's distribution, dominated by taxa with close references. For a real-run time estimate use gtdbtk_ani_screen_genbank/summary.json instead: 450 actual GenBank Enterobacterales genomes, 44 min, 5.3% fall-through.

Arm C spans 29 of the 57 phyla in the Bacteria pilot's taxonomy map, because only 4,193 of 22,871 genomes were retained with files on disk. Broad, but not the full breadth a whole-Bacteria run would place, so it disfavours rather than excludes a diversity effect on memory.

Arm C was stopped at 5h02m with 5 of up to 9 pplacer runs done, so its wall time is a lower bound. Its MEMORY peak is not: that fell at 17:24:59, inside the ANI window, before the first pplacer started.

Memory saturates with count rather than being constant -- 25 genomes cost 10.67 GiB. Nothing here measures below 25 or between 25 and 100, so the shape of the rise is unknown and only the plateau is established.

One machine, one GTDB release (226). The plateau and a 57 GiB box's ceiling would look alike on a single host; swap stayed at 0.33 GiB throughout, which argues against a ceiling, but a second machine would settle it.
recommendation: Keep 40 GB. It is measured, it is flat across every diversity tested, and it fixes the concurrency hazard by admission arithmetic. Re-measure before a whole-Bacteria run only if the ANI fall-through rate proves far higher than the 5.3% measured on real GenBank Enterobacterales -- and re-measure TIME rather than memory, which is the figure the arms could not pin down.
relationship_to_gtdbtk_headroom: THIS DID NOT DISCOVER THE MECHANISM -- gtdbtk_headroom/ did, and it is committed in this repo. That comparison measured 41.7 GB PSS in skani at t=449 s over 11 processes and recorded it as 'input-independent', 'set by sketching GTDB's 143,614 REFERENCE genomes' and 'the genuine memory ceiling ... at any input size'. 41.7 decimal GB is 38.8 GiB, which is the peak mem_used measured here to one decimal place -- an independent reproduction on a different input a month later. It also already recorded pplacer's 54.2 GB PSS and explained it as the file-backed scratch mapping rather than a requirement, which is the exact trap re-encountered here. The 4 GB figure in CLAUDE.md and main.nf therefore contradicted a committed comparison in this repo for two months, and the inconsistency was never caught. WHAT THIS ADDS: the DIVERSITY dimension, which gtdbtk_headroom did not vary (it changed only genome count); the pplacer-per-class-level-subtree time model; and the finding that a 60 s sampling interval is itself the reason the 4 GB figure was believable.
